inputs.share_count_basis: 2,800,312,865 shares in issue at 28 Feb 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, directors' interests note and EPS note 8). Diluted = basic: the EPS note states the outstanding Pre-IPO and Post-IPO share options were excluded because their adjusted exercise prices exceed the market price. Held flat; SBC is nil so there is nothing to double-count.
inputs.net_debt_note: 28 Feb 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, note 15 and balance sheet). Debt = bank and other borrowings and bonds RMB10,240m (current 2,953 + non-current 7,287; the RMB506m guaranteed bonds were repaid 20 Apr 2026 from cash, which does not change net debt) + lease liabilities RMB114m (21 current + 93 non-current). Cash reserve = cash and cash equivalents 3,589 + restricted bank deposits 79 (57 non-current + 22 current) + structured deposits held at FVTPL 1,479 = 5,147, the company's own 'cash reserve' definition. Net gearing on this basis 25.7% (18.4% at 31 Aug 2025).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement line 'Share-based payment expenses: -* (less than RMB1 million)' both years; FY2023 was RMB17m, FY2022 RMB20m. SBC-zero: rows kept at 0%, house and street bases coincide, band_position null.
inputs.fcf_note: reported_fcf = OCF 3,885 - payments for PP&E/right-of-use assets 2,952 (FY2025). Owner FCF 834 = 933 - 0 SBC - 99 interest income (investment income note 6(a), stripped because the whole cash reserve is netted in the bridge). FY2025 is NOT the base for the forward build: the flows are built from components anchored to adjusted EBITDA ex-interest (4,169 - 99 = 4,070, 55.3% of revenue) and the H1 FY2026 run-rate (2,028 - 46 = 1,982, 52.3%).
inputs.fx_note: CNY -> HKD 1.1721 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-10). All flows, EV, bridge and per-share values are built in RMB and converted to HKD at this rate for the quote-currency intrinsic values. No dual listing exists for a parity check; cross-check: market cap 2,800.3m x HK$1.92 = HK$5.38bn = RMB4.59bn, which the EV/EBITDA sanity multiple (EV ~RMB12bn / adj EBITDA ex-interest 4.07bn = ~2.9x) relies on. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-derive it on the next price refresh.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 = year ended 31 Aug 2025 (latest audited annual). Year 1 = FY2026 (ended 31 Aug 2026; results due late Nov 2026). Balance sheet and share count are the 28 Feb 2026 interim, six months newer than FY0 flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: 10-yr China Government Bond ~1.8%. Cost of equity ~10.5% = 1.8% + beta 1.35 x 6.5% (mature-market ERP 4.3% + China country premium ~0.9% + a size/liquidity component for a HK-listed mid-cap trading at ~3x EBITDA; beta reflects the HK-listed China private-education cohort). After-tax cost of debt 4.2% = ~5.6% (interest paid 577 / avg borrowings ~10.2bn; 80% variable-rate) x (1 - 25%). Capital structure 65/35 equity/debt on an intrinsic (not market) basis given gearing rising toward 26% and a RMB1.43bn ADB/AIIB facility still drawing: 0.65 x 10.5 + 0.35 x 4.2 = 8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Regulatory and enrolment risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario paths and a 30% bear weight -- the same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities RMB114m (28 Feb 2026) added to total_debt; lease principal (31) is NOT deducted from the flows; right-of-use depreciation (100 in FY2025) stays inside D&A; ongoing land-use-right/ROU additions are already in the capex line ('payments/deposits for acquisition of PP&E/right-of-use assets'). Immaterial either way: lease cash is ~0.5% of EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: NCI book value RMB2,295m (28 Feb 2026) deducted as an equity_bridge item; the flows are whole-company. Calibration: NCI share of profit was 84 (FY2024), 124 (H1 FY2025), 81 (H1 FY2026), i.e. ~10-17% of pre-impairment profit; 2,295 at book is ~10-14x that run-rate, in line with the group's own multiple. FY2025 NCI was -471 because RMB1,461m of the 1,706 impairment sat in the Hainan CGU where minorities hold a large stake -- that is why the CSV's attributable net_income (977) exceeds total profit (506).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US' + adaptations a/b/c/d/e). Recurring prepaid tuition from ~282k students; no bank/REIT/holdco characteristics; no live corporate action. NORMALISATION: FY2025 reported EBITDA 2,395 and operating profit are depressed by RMB1,706m of non-cash goodwill/intangible impairments (Hainan 1,461, Guangdong 122, Henan 123). The build anchors to adjusted EBITDA ex-interest income (4,070, 55.3%) stepped down to the H1 FY2026 run-rate (52.3%) rather than to the reported figure, so the impairment is neither carried forward nor added back as earnings; it is treated as a signal (regional overcapacity, enrolment +0.2% into 2025/26) that caps base-case growth at 3.5% and holds the bear weight at 30%. TAX: the cash tax rate is NOT the FY2025 effective ~14%; H1 FY2026 EIT rose from 159 to 345 (30% of PBT) as more schools are taxed at the 25% EIT rate, so the path starts at 26% of EBIT (bull 25%, bear 28%). CAPEX is the single largest judgment: FY2024 4,434 (67% of revenue), FY2025 2,952 (40%), H1 FY2026 1,458 (38%) against D&A of ~15%; the base tapers capex to 18% by year 8 (above D&A, i.e. continued modest expansion), the bear tapers slower (19% floor), the bull faster (16%). INTEREST INCOME 99 stripped from the flows because the matching asset (cash reserve 5,147 incl. structured deposits) is in the bridge; the ~12/yr fair-value gain on structured deposits inside adjusted EBITDA is left in (immaterial). LEVERAGE: gearing 25.7% and RMB2.9bn of net current liabilities, but interest cover ~8x on adj EBITDA; no refinancing stress modelled, charged through WACC weights not a scenario-specific premium. SBC is nil: house = street, band_position null. HORIZON 10 years because capex and the tax step are still normalising at year 5.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: H1 FY2026 revenue +3.2%, total enrolment +0.2% / higher-education +2.8% into the 2025/26 academic year; equity and revenue CAGRs reflect the 2019-2024 acquisition and campus build-out that has ended
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3-yr CAGR -16.9% vs revenue +15.7% and equity +6.1%: the divergence is the FY2024 (1,911) and FY2025 (1,706) impairments plus the FY2024-26 step-up in enterprise income tax, not a revenue problem. Equity 5-yr CAGR 14.3% includes the Jan-2021 HK$2.0bn top-up placing, not just retained earnings.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 -114, FY2021 -503, FY2022 501, FY2023 934, FY2024 -20, FY2025 834. 5-yr FCF CAGR is undefined (negative base). Reported FCF CAGR is identical in direction because SBC is nil; the only adjustment of size is interest income (61-101/yr). Revenue CAGRs are computed FY2022->FY2025 (3-yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5-yr); FY2018 is an 8-month stub after the Dec->Aug year-end change and is excluded from every CAGR.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA ex-interest income: FY2025 55.3%, H1 FY2026 52.3% (teacher investment, new-campus opex). Troughs at 52% then recovers only 1pp as new campuses fill.
base.capex_note: FY2025 40% / H1 FY2026 38% of revenue. Tapers to 18% (D&A 15.5%) -- continued expansion at a slower pace; the undeployed HK$2.0bn placing proceeds and ADB/AIIB facilities keep capex above maintenance through year 6.
base.cash_tax_note: H1 FY2026 EIT 345 on PBT 1,204 (~29%); 26% of EBIT assumes most schools at the 25% statutory rate with a small non-deductible margin.
base.wc_note: Contract liabilities were +814 in FY2024 but -25 in FY2025 on 12% revenue growth; 15% capture on the revenue CHANGE is a modest prepaid-tuition tailwind.
base.terminal_note: 2.0% terminal growth: tuition inflation offset by a shrinking college-age cohort from the mid-2030s. 15x cap (not the 20x compounder default) for a regulated, capex-heavy business.

scenario_narratives.base: Enrolment growth stays near zero in total but mixes toward higher-education and bachelor's programmes, so revenue grows 3-3.5% on tuition increases and mix, fading to 2.5%. The adjusted EBITDA margin troughs at 52% (H1 FY2026 run-rate) as teacher investment and new-campus opex are absorbed, recovering only to 53%. The step-up in enterprise income tax seen in H1 FY2026 is permanent (26% of EBIT). Capex, the key swing factor, tapers from 36% of revenue to 18% by year 8 as the current construction programme completes and the group stops adding capacity into regions where public providers are expanding; D&A rises to 16% then settles at 15.5%. No further impairments of the FY2024/FY2025 scale, but no reversal either. Regulation stays where it is: higher education remains 'restricted' on the Negative List but for-profit operation continues.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2024-2035 'Education Power' plan and employment-first policy translate into real demand for applied-degree and master's programmes; enrolment re-accelerates to mid-single digits with tuition increases on top (5-6% revenue growth for four years). International programmes (UK QAA-accredited, +18% new students) and Greater Bay Area campuses lift the margin to 56%. The capex cycle ends sooner (16% of revenue by year 7), the undeployed HK$2bn placing proceeds fund a bolt-on at a sector-trough multiple, and the group returns to a meaningful payout. Terminal 3%, 18x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2025 impairments were the leading edge: public universities keep expanding intake in Hainan, Guangdong and Henan, the secondary-vocational pipeline shrinks as provinces expand public high-school capacity, and the shrinking birth cohort arrives earlier than expected. Revenue declines 1-2% a year for four years and only stabilises at +1%; the margin falls to 45% because faculty costs and depreciation on RMB24bn of PP&E are fixed. Tax is 28%, working-capital tailwind zero, capex stays elevated longer because committed campus builds complete regardless. Terminal growth 1% and a 10x cap reflect a market that continues to price Chinese private education as a sector where cash may never reach shareholders (dividend cut to RMB82m in FY2025, 'development fund' appropriations, rising gearing). This scenario carries the regulatory tail: a tightening that restricts for-profit distributions would look like this path, not like a going-concern event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the business depends on a single regulator in a sector with a 2021 precedent for abrupt policy change, enrolment has decelerated to +0.2%, impairments have recurred two years running (1,911 then 1,706) and gearing rose 7pp in six months. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things (enrolment re-acceleration, an earlier end to the capex cycle, and a sector re-rating) to all go right. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A prepaid-tuition business with a 52-55% adjusted EBITDA margin on RMB7.4bn of revenue, trading at ~3x EV/EBITDA and ~3-4x normalised earnings because the market treats Chinese private higher education as un-investable after the 2021 K-12 crackdown and two years of campus impairments. The DCF values the cash the campuses can generate once the construction programme tapers; it does not assume a re-rating (the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF, not a sector multiple) but it does assume cash can eventually reach shareholders, which is the thesis a buyer is really underwriting. The 30% bear weight and bear path -- which values the equity below the current price -- is where the regulatory and demographic tail is charged.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory: a restriction on for-profit distributions or a reclassification of higher-education schools would trap cash inside the schools; the equity value is then a claim on assets, not on flows

Capex never tapers: management has built RMB10-12bn of campuses since FY2021 and has HK$2bn of undeployed placing proceeds plus ADB/AIIB facilities; if capex stays at 35-40% of revenue the base-case FCF does not materialise
Demographics and public-sector overcapacity in Hainan/Guangdong/Henan driving further impairments and negative enrolment growth (the bear path)
Tax rate: H1 FY2026 EIT was ~30% of PBT; a full 25% rate on every school plus indirect taxes could push the cash rate above the 26% modelled
Leverage: RMB10.2bn of borrowings, 80% variable-rate, RMB2.9bn net current liabilities; a refinancing squeeze would force higher-cost debt or an equity raise
FX: CNY/HKD moves pass straight through to the HKD intrinsic value; no hedging of USD/HKD/AUD borrowings
valuation_philosophy.no_rerate_memo: Approximate memo, not the house basis: holding the terminal value at today's ~3x EV/adjusted-EBITDA instead of the 15x FCF cap gives a base-case value in the region of HK$4 per share -- still roughly double the price. The gap between that and the house base value is the price of the thesis that the exit multiple normalises.
